input.question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".
input.ground_truth: It isn't just "goat cheese", it's just that your average American doesn't have enough experiences with goat cheeses to name any particular one. Feta, Kunik, Castelo Branco, and Clochette are all (at least partially) goat cheese that I've eaten personally. I'd think that pretty much everyone in the US has some experience with feta at a minimum.

Question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of Legos that are all the same color. You can build *lots* of different things with them—houses, cars, castles! That's like cow's milk cheese. People have made cheese from cow's milk for a very long time in many places, so they made *lots* of different kinds. Some are soft, some are hard, some are smelly, some are mild.

Now, imagine you have a small box of Legos that are a different color. Maybe you only have a few pieces. You just call them "the green Legos" and build whatever you can with them. That's like goat's milk cheese. Not as many people have made cheese from goat's milk for so long, or maybe goats give less milk. So, people just call it "goat cheese" and don't make as many different kinds.

But both kinds of cheese are yummy! 🧀🐐🐄
